summary: A compact, playable beat with a clean turn from sleepy teasing to contained dread. The letters reveal affection and fear without exposition, and Sayed’s restraint keeps the familiar death-letter device grounded.

lines.speaker: MOSTAFA

performance.delivery: Read the words as he writes them, in a young man’s full chest voice. Keep the letter formula natural and let the pauses, not sentimentality, reveal his fear.

lines.text: «أُمِّي الْغَالْيَةْ… أَنَا بِخِيرْ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهْ. مَا تِقْلَقِيشْ عَلَيَّا…»

lines.speaker: ADEL

performance.delivery: Speak without fully lifting his head from the pack. The teasing is habitual barracks warmth, not a performance for the other men.

lines.text: بِتِكْتِبْ لِمِينْ يَا مُصْطَفَى؟ لِلْبِتّْ اللِّي فِي الْبَلَدْ؟

performance.delivery: Answer without looking up or interrupting the pencil. Keep it simple and unembarrassed; the single word should make Adel’s joke fall away.
Let the grin disappear before speaking. Address Mostafa softly, then retreat into the pack as though the mention of a mother has touched something private.

lines.speaker: SAYED
issues: «لَوْ مَا رِجِعْتِشْ» is a familiar war-drama death flag; restrained delivery is essential to keep it from feeling prewritten.

performance.delivery: Hold the folded page out to Mostafa and speak as if assigning an ordinary chore. Do not catch the voice or seek sympathy; the effort to stay practical is the emotion.

lines.text: خُدْ دَهْ. لَوْ مَا رِجِعْتِشْ… وَصَّلُهْ لِفَاطْمَةْ بِإِيدَكْ.

lines.speaker: MOSTAFA
issues: «يَا عَمّْ سَيِّدْ» is informal for a private addressing his sergeant; it works because this is a private, filial exchange rather than a report or order.

performance.delivery: Look up immediately and reject the possibility before thinking. Keep the voice weighted and adult, with the upset compressed so the sleeping men are not disturbed.
Close the argument without looking for reassurance. Soften only slightly on «مَعَاكْ», then make «وِخَلَاصْ» a firm full stop.
